findings.summary: The scanner's runtime-root fallback diverges from the engine's own: loop-engine's runtimeRoot() (src/lib/runtime-root.ts:25-32) ends at ~/.loop-engine, while this default ends at /data/loop-engine. Branches 1-3 (LOOP_ENGINE_RUNTIME_ROOT, ~/.config/loop-engine/config.json, LOOP_ENGINE_STATE) are identical, and the spec's measured production evidence (index at /data/loop-engine/index.jsonl, run_dirs under /data/loop-engine/runs/) confirms production resolves to /data/loop-engine, so the prior attempt's blocker is genuinely fixed. But in an environment with no config and no env vars, writer and reader would disagree, yielding a false 'no lane entries' exit 3. The failure is loud and named rather than silent, so it does not violate the spec's prohibition. Deriving the root from the drain JSON's own runs_root (already captured in DRAIN_TMP) would remove the env-resolution coupling entirely.

Three pre-scan guards exit 0 silently: empty stdin, unparseable stdin, and missing/non-string drain_id. On the real path a drain that exited 0 always prints exactly one JSON line containing drain_id (loop-engine src/cli.ts:778/798), and the spec's loud-failure mandate names only index.jsonl and journal.jsonl, so no acceptance criterion is broken today. Still, these are exactly the 'treat an unreadable trace as no failure' shape the package exists to eliminate; if drain's stdout contract ever changes, tick failures would go invisible again with exit 0 and no diagnostic.

Y5's quoted `git diff --stat` lists only scripts/check-drain-failures.mjs (+1/-1) without stating its base. Read as the incremental rework diff against the previous attempt it is plausible and truthful (attempt 2's fix was the one-line default-root change), and the full package diff is likewise confined to this repo (bin/, scripts/, test/, docs/) with loop-engine untouched, so Y5's substance holds. But because the base is unstated, the evidence reads as if it were the whole change and cannot be interpreted unambiguously by a reviewer. The prior continuous review raised the same point.

The Y4 reachability declaration cites the wrong killing assertion for one of the two mutations it names. Under an 'uncaught readFileSync throw' mutation, node still exits non-zero, so `expect(res.code).not.toBe(0)` would pass; what actually kills that mutation is `expect(res.err).toContain("not found")`, since an ENOENT stack trace says 'no such file or directory'. The test therefore does have the required discriminating power, and the declaration's other named mutation (silent pass) is correctly attributed — only the stated reasoning is imprecise.
